title: How are people using Astra to make video games?
author: Hockless
selftext: Is it just the case of hooking it up to Unreal/Unity?

comments.author: aicis
comments.body:
For dumb prototypes you can just prompt it.

For a real project you will need to establish some workflows, guardrails, etc. I don't think there is one golden rule how to do that, everyone has their own setup.

comments.author: -qix
comments.body:
Pretty much. Once you’ve got the game project on your machine you can just point ChatGPT/Claude/VS code to it and then speak to the agent as you would normally. 

What I always do for games is make a GDD markdown file first. Make it detailed and include phases and stages for development. Then when starting in chat. Ask it to use that document and create its own dev task list.

Ask it to update this task list as it goes on and get it to also make notes on how certain things work. This will make coming back to a chat much easier when running out of usage or switching model / platform.

There are lots of skills you can give it that can save its time researching. Like there will be a u it’s skill, a godot skill etc. these are good but not required. They just save tokens nowadays.

Speaking of saving tokens I would also learn the caveman skill: Makes Claude speak like this, so no detail, straight to point. Save many tokens. Same performance.

Also I’d have a look at godot before using other platforms like Unity. Godot is lightweight and very beginner friendly.
